**Arrange on the bed** puts the objects side by side and starts a new plate as soon as the current one is full. What does not fit even then is not dropped, it is reported.

**Too big for the bed?** *Split automatically* cuts until every piece fits. The parting plane is searched for, not guessed, two dowels go into every cut face, and each cut stays a number you can change afterwards.

**Export goes to STL, 3MF or STEP.** 3MF is what slicers prefer, and it carries the material slots along as colour groups; STL knows no colour and loses them accordingly. STEP exists for exact bodies, with real faces and edges.

**The slicer stays outside.** The layer analysis searches and judges — islands, spans, thin spots, the best orientation — but the print file is written by the slicer. Wherever both give numbers, which one comes from where is always stated.

The piece that sets Formwerk apart from a slicer.

**The clearance is in the material profile, not in the model.** To put a pin into a hole you do not enter 0.2 — you say *fit*, and the number comes from the profile of the material being printed.

**That is why calibrating works backwards.** Under *Edit → Calibrate material* the measured value is entered. From then on it applies to every fit — including those in projects that existed before.

**Measured is printed, not guessed.** The *tolerance ladder* puts pins and holes with stepped clearance on one plate: print once, try, and the value stands. The *wall ladder* and the *overhang fan* do the same for the minimum wall thickness and for the angle at which this printer really needs supports — instead of the rule of thumb of 45 degrees.

**The test piece** cuts a cube out around one spot instead of rebuilding it. What gets printed is the real geometry with the real tolerance: two minutes instead of two hours, and the result holds for the part.

**A scene may have several materials.** A TPU gasket in a PETG housing shrinks differently and wants more clearance. With *set material* the single body gets its own profile, and tolerances, elephant foot and fit checking compute with it.

Fast jede Aufgabe geht einen von drei We:
Almost every task takes one of three ways. An example project is ready for each — on the start screen, to open and look through.

**Way 1 — adapt somebody else's model.** Something downloaded that almost fits: read it in, repair it, drill it, export it. The most common way, and the one where the repair matters.

**Way 2 — build it yourself.** Something new out of primitives and building blocks, with named parameters: width, depth, thickness. Change a number and the part changes.

**Way 3 — clean up a generated model.** What an image model delivers is a surface, not a construction. It goes through the repair chain, and holes and fits are steps of their own afterwards — not something you get by measuring the mesh.

Formwerk baut, ändert und druckreif mach:
Formwerk builds, changes and print-readies models for the 3D printer.

Three things set it apart from what else is open:

* **Every step stays a number.** A hole two millimetres off gets moved, not drilled again.
* **Fits come from the material, not from a feeling.** Measure your clearance once and you improve parts you built before.
* **Building blocks instead of handwork.** Nut trap, heat-set insert, latch, living hinge, magnet pocket — one click each instead of half an hour each.

**What it is not:** no CAD replacement — there are no sketches and no constraints. No slicer — the print file still comes from the slicer, Formwerk only searches and judges. No cloud — no account, no telemetry, nothing that leaves the machine.

Without a network, without an account and without a language model, everything except the chat stays usable.

Jede Operation steht im Verlauf, und dor:
Every operation stands in the history, and there it stays editable.

**Double-click a step** to open it again — with the values that are in the file. To move a hole two millimetres, change the number; only what hangs below it is recomputed.

**Undo takes back a whole transaction**, not half a step. A chat proposal is exactly one transaction — an undo takes it back completely.

Two limits are deliberate. Steps that were taken back fall away as soon as a new one arrives: there are no branches. And a change that alters the *number* of objects while later steps work with them is refused — the new bodies are not the old ones, and an error at the end caused by a number at the start is one nobody can trace back.

**Clicking sets the place.** Select a face in the window, then call an operation, and place and axis are already filled in. The size is not: a countersink takes the head of the screw, not the diameter of the hole it sits on.
Jede Operation über ihren Namen finden,: Find any operation by name, without walking the menus.
